name: AL-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+33 partisan lean in a deeply conservative northwest Alabama district
Aderholt is a long-tenured incumbent with a large financial edge
Democratic challenger raised only ~$16K with negligible cash on hand
model.rationale: Aderholt holds a seat with an R+33 lean, has out-raised his challenger roughly 65-to-1, and prediction markets give Democrats essentially no chance. Nothing in the evidence suggests anything other than a comfortable Republican win.
model.watch: Only a major late scandal or incumbent retirement-level surprise could move this race, and neither is in evidence.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northwest Alabama's 4th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of R+33. Robert Aderholt, first elected in 1996, is seeking another term and has built a campaign warchest of about $750,000. His Democratic opponent, Amanda Pusczek, has raised roughly $16,000 and reported under $400 on hand, leaving her with no realistic capacity to compete on air or in the field.

No public polls or expert ratings target the race, but prediction markets price a Republican win at near-certainty. The fundamentals point to a lopsided result, with the only real question being the size of Aderholt's margin rather than the outcome.
